name: Heiwadai
tagline: Shinjuku in 26 minutes and Shibuya in 31 minutes. Served by 2 lines. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥70,000 to ¥80,000.
summary: The station is in Nerima City, where Tokyo Metro run 2 lines between them. Journey times to the main business districts are 36 minutes to Otemachi, 26 minutes to Shinjuku, 31 minutes to Shibuya and 52 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥70,000 to ¥80,000. The station stands 35 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 1.2 m. The land around the station is close to level.

terrain.note: The station sits on the higher side of the ground around it, at 35 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 34.4 m to 35.6 m, a difference of 1.2 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls outside the projected inundation area. Of the nine points within 400 m of the station, 3 fall inside the area, and the deepest projection among them is 0.5 to 3 m. The projected depth differs block by block within the same station area, so check the ward hazard map for the specific address. Inland flooding from overwhelmed drains has no nationwide map; each ward publishes its own, and that is worth reading as well.

medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 4 clinics and 6 pharmacies. The nearest hospital is 練馬光が丘病院, about 31 minutes' walk from the station. The next nearest is 東京武蔵野病院, about 38 minutes' walk. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 2 lines serve the station. Tokyo Metro Yurakucho Line run through it. Tokyo Metro Fukutoshin Line also call here. Both lines are run by Tokyo Metro, so a fault affecting that company can stop them together.
congestion: Tokyo Metro Yurakucho Line runs at 153% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch is 東池袋→護国寺, which this station is not on. Tokyo Metro Fukutoshin Line runs at 117%. Its busiest stretch is 要町→池袋, which this station is likewise not on. At 150%, the ministry's scale describes shoulders not quite touching, with crowding near the doors. The figures describe each line's busiest stretch, so the stretch you ride may be easier.

rentRange.note: One room ¥70,000 to ¥80,000, 1K ¥80,000 to ¥90,000, 1LDK ¥130,000 to ¥140,000 and 2LDK ¥170,000 to ¥180,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.

leads.terrain: The ground around the station is almost level, so you can choose where to live without thinking about slopes.
leads.groceries: There are 5 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 2 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: Among the 23 wards' stations, comparatively few of the points around this one fall inside the projected inundation area for the largest rainfall the government models.
leads.stationNote: 2 lines serve the station. The choice of connections is about average for the 23 wards.
leads.rentRange: Set against how long the commute takes, rents here are on the low side.
leads.medical: The number of clinics and pharmacies within walking distance is on the low side for the 23 wards.
leads.congestion: Morning loading on the lines here is about average for the 23 wards' stations.
